options: A Large Language Model trained on huge amounts of text

Because words cannot be stored in computers

questions.question: Scientists created Artificial Neural Networks primarily to mimic which natural system?
questions.explanation: Artificial Neural Networks are inspired by the way biological neurons in the human brain connect and transmit signals.

questions.question: If a neural network has only an input layer and output layer with no hidden layers, it is least capable of:
questions.explanation: Hidden layers allow networks to learn complex features. Without them, the model cannot capture complex patterns.

questions.question: In Deep Learning, why are multiple hidden layers useful?
options: They allow AI to learn patterns in increasing complexity
They prevent training data from being used
They convert images to text automatically
questions.correctAnswer: They allow AI to learn patterns in increasing complexity
questions.explanation: Different hidden layers progressively detect basic to complex features.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how a CNN processes an image?
options: It reads the entire image as a single word
It converts the image into audio signals
It scans pixel grids using filters to detect patterns
It memorizes every pixel without processing
questions.correctAnswer: It scans pixel grids using filters to detect patterns
questions.explanation: CNN filters slide across pixel grids detecting patterns like edges and shapes.

questions.question: Which task is most suitable for a CNN?
options: Predicting the next word in a sentence
questions.explanation: CNNs specialize in analyzing visual patterns in images.

questions.question: What special feature allows an RNN to remember previous information?
questions.explanation: RNNs include loops that allow information to persist across time steps.

questions.question: Which type of data is BEST suited for RNN processing?
questions.explanation: RNNs are designed to process ordered sequences like sentences or time data.

questions.question: Why do traditional RNNs struggle with very long sequences?
options: They lose earlier information over time
questions.correctAnswer: They lose earlier information over time
questions.explanation: RNNs suffer from short-term memory issues and forget earlier parts of long sequences.

questions.question: Which major AI architecture solved many long-sequence problems of RNNs?
questions.explanation: Transformers process entire sequences simultaneously and maintain relationships between words.

questions.question: The attention mechanism helps AI mainly by:
options: Focusing on important words and relationships
questions.correctAnswer: Focusing on important words and relationships
questions.explanation: Attention assigns importance to key words so AI understands context better.

questions.question: In machine learning, what is the purpose of training data?
questions.explanation: Training data allows the model to learn relationships between inputs and outputs.

questions.question: Why must testing data be different from training data?
options: To prevent memorization from appearing as learning
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent memorization from appearing as learning
questions.explanation: Testing with unseen data ensures the model actually learned general rules.

questions.question: A model that performs perfectly on training data but poorly on new data is suffering from:
questions.explanation: Overfitting occurs when the model memorizes training data rather than learning patterns.

questions.question: Which scenario best represents underfitting?
options: AI cannot identify even obvious examples
AI perfectly predicts all training data
questions.correctAnswer: AI cannot identify even obvious examples
questions.explanation: Underfitting means the model failed to learn enough patterns.

questions.question: Which fitting scenario indicates ideal learning?
questions.explanation: Perfect fitting means the model generalizes well to unseen data.

questions.question: Which metric simply measures the percentage of correct predictions?
questions.explanation: Accuracy is the proportion of total predictions that are correct.

questions.question: Precision primarily evaluates:
options: How many predicted positives are correct
questions.correctAnswer: How many predicted positives are correct
questions.explanation: Precision measures correctness among predicted positive results.

questions.question: Recall focuses on:
questions.explanation: Recall measures how many real positive cases the AI successfully identifies.

questions.question: Why is F1 Score useful?
questions.explanation: F1 Score combines precision and recall into a single balanced metric.

questions.question: A loss function mainly tells us:
questions.explanation: Loss measures the distance between predictions and correct answers.

questions.question: Which feature distinguishes an AI Agent from traditional AI?
options: It interacts with environments to achieve goals
questions.correctAnswer: It interacts with environments to achieve goals
questions.explanation: Agents actively observe, decide, and act to achieve objectives.

questions.question: The three-step agent loop consists of:
questions.explanation: This loop continuously guides agent behavior.

questions.question: In an AI Agent, sensors belong to which component?
questions.explanation: Inputs allow agents to observe their environment.

questions.question: In AI agents, the Brain primarily performs:
questions.explanation: The brain processes inputs and chooses optimal actions.

questions.question: In a digital AI agent, sending an automated email would be an example of:
questions.explanation: Output actions change the environment.

questions.question: Large Language Models are mainly built using which architecture?
questions.explanation: Modern LLMs rely on transformer architectures with attention mechanisms.

questions.question: What does an LLM primarily learn from large datasets?
options: How words relate and form language patterns
questions.correctAnswer: How words relate and form language patterns
questions.explanation: LLMs learn statistical relationships in human language.

questions.question: Why do LLMs use tokens instead of full words?
options: To reduce vocabulary rigidity and understand new words
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce vocabulary rigidity and understand new words
questions.explanation: Tokenization allows flexible understanding of new and complex words.

questions.question: Approximately how many characters are usually represented by one token?
questions.explanation: On average, one token represents about four English characters.

questions.question: What limits how much information an LLM can process at once?
questions.explanation: Context window defines the maximum tokens the model can remember simultaneously.

questions.question: If an input exceeds the context window, the AI will:
questions.explanation: LLMs cannot retain tokens beyond their context window limit.

questions.question: Prompt engineering mainly focuses on:
questions.explanation: Better prompts lead to more accurate AI outputs.

questions.question: KV Cache improves LLM performance mainly by:
options: Avoiding repeated processing of previous tokens
questions.correctAnswer: Avoiding repeated processing of previous tokens
questions.explanation: KV cache stores previous attention results so the model doesn't recompute them.

questions.question: KV Cache can be compared to:
questions.explanation: It stores previously processed information for quick reference.

questions.question: What is HuggingFace primarily known for?
options: Hosting open-source AI models and datasets
questions.correctAnswer: Hosting open-source AI models and datasets
questions.explanation: HuggingFace is a platform where developers share machine learning models and tools.

questions.question: In an Artificial Neural Network, what is the primary role of digital nodes?
options: Pass mathematical signals to other nodes
questions.correctAnswer: Pass mathematical signals to other nodes
questions.explanation: Nodes in neural networks pass weighted mathematical signals to connected nodes to process information.

questions.question: In Deep Learning architecture, the hidden layers primarily perform which function?
questions.explanation: Hidden layers progressively learn features from simple to complex.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly represents the information flow in a deep neural network?
questions.explanation: Data enters through the input layer, is processed in hidden layers, and produces results in the output layer.

questions.question: What would most likely happen if a CNN used no filters when processing images?
options: It could not detect visual patterns
It would behave like an RNN
questions.correctAnswer: It could not detect visual patterns
questions.explanation: Filters are essential for detecting edges, shapes, and patterns in images.

questions.question: Which AI system would most likely rely heavily on CNN technology?
questions.explanation: CNNs specialize in analyzing visual data such as faces.

questions.question: Which property of RNNs allows them to process sequences such as sentences?
questions.explanation: Loops allow RNNs to retain information from previous steps.

questions.question: A major limitation of traditional RNNs when processing very long text is:
questions.explanation: RNNs suffer from memory limitations that cause earlier sequence information to fade.

questions.question: Transformers improved AI language understanding mainly because they:
options: Process sequences strictly one word at a time
questions.explanation: Transformers analyze relationships between all words at once.

questions.question: The attention mechanism helps an AI primarily determine:
options: Which words are most important for meaning
questions.correctAnswer: Which words are most important for meaning
questions.explanation: Attention assigns importance to words depending on context.

questions.question: In machine learning workflows, the main reason for separating training and testing datasets is to:
options: Prevent memorization from appearing as learning
questions.correctAnswer: Prevent memorization from appearing as learning
questions.explanation: Testing with unseen data confirms genuine learning.

questions.question: If an AI model predicts dogs correctly only when trees appear in the background because training data contained trees, the model suffers from:
questions.explanation: The model memorized irrelevant patterns in training data.

questions.question: Which situation best represents underfitting in an AI model?
questions.explanation: Underfitting occurs when the model has not learned enough.

questions.question: Which metric would be most affected if an AI frequently predicts "yes" incorrectly?
questions.explanation: Precision measures correctness among predicted positive cases.

questions.question: Which metric focuses on how many real positive cases were correctly detected?
questions.explanation: Recall measures how many actual positive cases were found.

questions.question: Why is the F1 score considered more balanced than accuracy?
questions.explanation: F1 Score balances the trade-off between precision and recall.

questions.question: In training AI models, the loss function primarily guides:
questions.explanation: Loss functions quantify errors so models can adjust parameters.

questions.question: Which characteristic uniquely defines an AI Agent?
questions.explanation: Agents actively interact with environments to achieve goals.

questions.question: In the agent loop, which step immediately follows observation?
questions.explanation: After observing the environment, the agent decides the best action.

questions.question: In an AI agent, a camera attached to a robot functions as:
questions.explanation: Sensors provide environmental data to the agent.

questions.question: Which of the following would be considered an output action for a digital AI agent?
questions.explanation: Output actions change the external environment.

questions.question: Large Language Models are trained on extremely large text datasets mainly to:
questions.explanation: LLMs learn relationships between words and phrases.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a token in language models?
questions.explanation: Tokens are smaller units that language models process.

questions.question: Why does tokenization help AI understand new words or slang?
options: It breaks words into reusable pieces
questions.correctAnswer: It breaks words into reusable pieces
questions.explanation: Subword tokens allow AI to interpret unfamiliar words.

questions.question: Which factor limits the maximum length of text an LLM can process at once?
questions.explanation: Context window defines how many tokens the model can handle simultaneously.

questions.question: If an LLM processes text exceeding its context window, it will most likely:
questions.explanation: Tokens beyond the window limit cannot remain in working memory.

questions.question: Prompt engineering improves AI outputs mainly by:
questions.explanation: Well-designed prompts guide AI responses effectively.

questions.question: KV Cache improves generation speed because it:
questions.explanation: KV Cache saves previous attention calculations.

questions.question: The 'sticky note' analogy for KV Cache refers to:
questions.explanation: KV cache keeps key-value pairs from earlier tokens.

questions.question: Which platform is widely used by AI researchers to share models and datasets?
questions.explanation: HuggingFace hosts open-source ML models, datasets, and tools.

questions.question: Which scenario best represents the future vision of AI agents described in the content?
options: AI automatically planning events and executing tasks
questions.correctAnswer: AI automatically planning events and executing tasks
questions.explanation: Future AI agents will autonomously observe, decide, and act to complete complex tasks.
